title: Zuri and the Vanishing Puddle
markdown:
Sunny Meadow Playground had a special chalk-drawn puddle map. Zuri loved it. The lines were bright, the puddle was a perfect silver oval, and Bloop the robot had already beeped a proud little inventory of every path, including the one that went around the oak and the one that pretended to be a river.

But one sunny morning, the puddle and her map were gone. “Oh no!” Zuri whispered. Bloop whirred sadly, lights dimming as if the missing water had taken his batteries too. Coach Ellis, with a smile as warm as sunshine, said, “A puzzle, isn’t it?”

The sun shone warm on Zuri’s cheeks. She saw dewdrops on the grass. They sparkled, then seemed to melt and disappear. They didn’t drip. They just vanished, as if the grass had finished a drink nobody saw. Zuri’s eyes widened. “Do you think the sun took our map?” she whispered to Coach Ellis.

Coach Ellis asked, “Why do you think that?”

Zuri explained, her voice excited. “The dewdrops vanish when the sun shines! And the air feels damp, like the water went up! Maybe our map dried up and flew away!”

Bloop beeped happily. “Boop! Like magic!”

Zuri grinned. “Not magic, Bloop! It’s science! It’s called evaporation!”

Coach Ellis clapped gently. “You discovered a scientific principle, Zuri. The sun’s warmth turned water into invisible vapour, and it rose into the sky.”

Zuri’s mind buzzed. She looked at the stones and leaves, which were still stubbornly themselves, not vanishing just because the sun had opinions. “We can’t make a chalk map that disappears!” she declared. With Coach Ellis’s help, they gathered stones to outline a map and colourful leaves for paths. Zuri carefully placed them, pressing each stone until it sat like a period at the end of a sentence. Bloop handed her the reddest leaf as if it were a treasure. This new map wouldn’t disappear.

Bloop let out happy beeps. Zuri smiled. “It’s evaporation. When water gets warm, it turns into an invisible gas and floats up. That’s why puddles dry up and wet clothes get dry.”

Coach Ellis beamed. “And it’s why we have clouds and rain for new puddles.”

Zuri looked at the sky, where yesterday’s puddle might already be practising being a cloud. Who could have guessed water could fly away? The trees seemed to nod. Zuri, her mind buzzing with discoveries, couldn’t wait to find more secrets hidden in plain sight—especially if the next one started as a puddle and ended as weather.
characters: Zuri (careful coder), Bloop (whirring robot), Ellis (sunshine-warm coach)
author: StoryGen Community
